Name: Average temperature
Definition: Seasonal average temperature
Commentary: Like TMm, but for seasonal instead of daily mean temperatures

Name: Minimum temperature
Definition: Seasonal average minimum temperature
Commentary: Like TNm, but for seasonal instead of daily min temperatures

Name: Maximum temperature
Definition: Seasonal average maximum temperature
Commentary: Like TXm, but for seasonal instead of daily max temperatures

Name: Rainfall
Definition: Seasonal total rainfall
Commentary: If using pr, requires aux data like temperature to control for solid phase

Name: Record-breaking weather (hottest day)
Definition: Number of days per year at least as hot as the hottest day (Tmax) between 1981 and 2010
Commentary: In relation to max(TXx over 1981-2010)

Name: Record-breaking weather (hottest month)
Definition: Number of months per year at least as hot as the hottest month (Tmax) between 1981 and 2010

Name: Record-breaking weather (wettest month)
Definition: Number of months per year at least as wet as the wettest month between 1981 and 2010

Name: Met Office heatwave
Definition: Occurrence of heatwave following Met Office definition: heatwave threshold is met when a location records a period of at least three consecutive days with daily maximum temperatures meeting or exceeding the heatwave temperature threshold [set between 25 (most of the country) and 28 (London and certain surrounding counties)]. Definitions valid only for the UK.

Name: Amber heat-health alert
Definition: Occurrence of a public health heat-health alert: potential warning if medium heat-health alert thresholds reached for maximum daytime temperature (32.0°C to 39.9°C for London, 30.0°C to 37.0°C for other areas) and night-time temperature (95th percentile or higher of summer "nights"). Definitions valid only for the UK.

Name: Cold weather alert
Definition: Occurrence of a public health cold weather alert: potential warning if daily mean temperature below 2.0°C for 5 days AND below 0.0°C for 48hrs or more. Definitions valid only for the UK.

Name: Very hot days
Definition: Days with maximum temperature above 35°C

Name: Tropical nights
Definition: Days with minimum temperature above 20°C

Name: Heat stress
Definition: Days with shade Wet Bulb Globe Temperature (WBGT) above 25
AssociatedVariable: tas, sfcWind, huss, rss, psl (air temperature at surface, surface wind, specific humidity, net surface shortwave flux, surface pressure at sea level)
Commentary: This paper describes similar derivation of WBGT for climate projections: https://doi.org/10.1007/s00484-024-02776-5

Name: Heating degree days
Definition: Average annual heating degree days: relative to 15.5°C and 18°C

Name: Cooling degree days
Definition: Average annual cooling degree days: relative to 18°C and 22°C

Name: Road melt risk
Definition: Days with Tmax above 25°C

Name: Road accident risk
Definition: Days with Tmin below 0°C

Name: Rail: high temperatures
Definition: Days with Tmax above thresholds (>21, 24, 26, 30°C)

Name: Rail: bad weather days
Definition: Days with temperature, rainfall and/or windspeed beyond thresholds (not defined)

Name: Start of crop growing season
Definition: First day of first five-day period with average temperature above 5.6°C

Name: Growing season length
Definition: Length between start and end of growing season

Name: Growing degree days
Definition: Accumulated degree-days relative to 5.6°C

Name: Crop growth duration
Definition: Time to accumulate the 1981-2010 average growing degree days

Name: Start of field operations (Tsum200)
Definition: Day when accumulated temperatures above 0°C reach 200°C

Name: Accumulated frost
Definition: Sum of minimum temperatures below 0°C

Name: Frost days
Definition: Days with Tmin below 0°C

Name: Dairy cattle heat stress
Definition: Days with a Temperature Humidity Index above 70.

Name: Wheat heat stress
Definition: Days between 1 May and 15 June with maximum temperature above 32°C

Name: Potential Soil Moisture Deficit
Definition: Average annual maximum cumulative difference between rainfall and potential evaporation
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot (potential evaporation/CF: water_potential_evaporation_flux). Potential evaporation can be calculated using huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Based on Hannaford et al. (2023): https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-15-2391-2023

Name: Days above field capacity
Definition: Number of days with soil moisture at or above field capacity
AssociatedVariable: mrso (mass_content_of_water_in_soil), mrsofc (soil_moisture_content_at_field_capacity) or calculate using land surface model: pr, tas, huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, psl
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: SPI drought
Definition: Number of months with a Standardised Precipitation Index (calculated from 3-month accumulated rainfall) less than -1.5.

Name: SPEI drought
Definition: Number of months with a Standardised Precipitation Evaporation Index (calculated from 6-month accumulated rainfall minus potential evaporation) less than -1.5.

Name: Met Office Fire Danger
Units: Days/year; % chance greater than the current mean
Definition: Days with the MOFSI index above specific thresholds: >17.35 for very high, >52.538 for exception. Definitions valid only for the UK.
Commentary: Calculation based on Canadian Forest Fire Weather Index and described in detail in: Arnell et al. (2021) https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/abd9f2

Name: Wildfire: Daily Hazard Assessment
Units: Days/year; % chance greater than the current mean
Definition: Days with MOFSI components above specific thresholds. Components are FFMC (Fine Fuel Moisture Code), ISI (Initial Spread Index), DMC (Duff Moisture Code), DC (Drought Code) and FWI (Fire Weather Index). Thresholds are season-specific and available for FFMC, ISI, and FWI. Relates to amber and red warning conditions. An ‘amber’ warning level means that severe wildfire conditions are forecast with a likelihood of difficult-to-control wildfires. The ‘red’ level means extreme wildfire conditions are forecast, and occurs when the amber thresholds are passed and other weather conditions are conducive to fire (persistent high temperatures, low humidity and high windspeeds).
Commentary: Described in detail in Arnell et al. (2021) https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/abd9f3
LinkedIndicators: Met Office Fire Danger; Wildfire: FFMC 99th percentile; Fire Weather Index

Name: Wildfire: FFMC 99th percentile
Definition: Days with Fine Fuel Moisture Code component of MOFSI above the 99th percentile over the period 1981-2010, calculated by season. FFMC index represents the availability of dry ‘tinder’ material in and around the vegetation susceptible to ignition.
Commentary: Described in detail in Arnell et al. (2021) https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/abd9f4
LinkedIndicators: Met Office Fire Danger; Wildfire: Daily Hazard Assessment; Fire Weather Index

Name: River runoff
Definition: Annual and seasonal river runoff
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: River flood (2-year return period)
Definition: Magnitude of the 2-year flood
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: River flood (5-year return period)
Definition: Magnitude of the 5-year flood
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: River flood (10-year return period)
Definition: Magnitude of the 10-year flood
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: River flood (likelihood of current 10-year event)
Definition: Likelihood of the 10-year flood
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model
LinkedIndicators: River flood; River flood (10-year return period)

Name: Low flows (2-year return period)
Definition: Change in the 2-year lowest 7-day average river flow
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: Low flows (10-year return period)
Definition: Change in the 10-year lowest 7-day average river flow
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: Low flows (likelihood of current 10-year event)
Definition: Likelihood of 20-year low river flows
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: 12-month river drought (extreme)
Definition: Number of months with a Standardised Streamflow Index (calculated from 12-month accumulated river flow) less than -1.5.
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: 12-month river drought (severe)
Definition: Number of months with a Standardised Streamflow Index (calculated from 12-month accumulated river flow) less than-2.0.
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: 24-month river drought (extreme)
Definition: Number of months with a Standardised Streamflow Index (calculated from 24-month accumulated river flow) less than -1.5.
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: 24-month river drought (severe)
Definition: Number of months with a Standardised Streamflow Index (calculated from 24-month accumulated river flow) less than -2.0.
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsblpot / huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, tas, psl, pr
Commentary: Calculated using hydrological model

Name: Soil moisture
Definition: Average seasonal soil moisture content
AssociatedVariable: mrso (Mass Content Of Water In Soil) or calculate using land surface model: pr, tas, huss, rls, rss, sfcWind, psl
Commentary: Can be calculated by land surface model like in Szczykulska et al. (2024) https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ad7045

Name: Warmest Three-Day Period
Definition: The highest daily mean temperature averaged over a three-day window over a period (°C). In weather and climate models temperature is the variable simulating atmospheric air temperature at 2m above the surface. This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly values over a reference period.

Name: Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days
Definition: The Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days Index (Number of Days) is defined as a period of at least two consecutive days during the summer months (June, July, August) in which both the daily apparent temperature and the daily minimum temperature exceed their monthly 90th percentiles defined over a reference period. Apparent temperature is a linear function of temperature and dew point temperature to account for humidity conditions.

Name: Climatological Heatwave Days
Definition: The count of days under climatological heatwaves conditions (Number of days). A climatological heatwave is a period of at least three consecutive days exceeding the 99th percentile of the daily maximum temperatures of the May to September season during a reference period.

Name: High UTCI Days
Definition: The UTCI is an equivalent temperature (°C) and is a measure of the human physiological response to meteorological conditions that also takes into consideration the clothing adaptation of the population in response to outdoor temperature. It is based on four surface variables: air temperature, relative humidity, wind speed and mean radiant temperature. UTCI values are divided in 5 classes of heat stress: no thermal stress (9°C-26°C), moderate heat stress (26°C-32°C), strong heat stress (32°C-38°C), very strong heat stress (38C°-46C°), and extreme heat stress (>46°C). The index refers to the number of days in the category of strong heat stress or stronger (>32°C).

Name: Total Precipitation
Definition: The cumulated precipitation over a period (mm/period). In weather and climate models total precipitation is the flux of water equivalent (rain or snow) reaching the land surface (expressed as kg⋅m⁻²⋅sec⁻² and converted to mm/day). This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly cumulated values over the considered period.

Name: Mean Temperature
Definition: The mean of 2m temperature (°C) values during a given period. In weather and climate models temperature is the variable simulating atmospheric air temperature at 2m above the surface. This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly values over a reference period.
Commentary: Like TMm, but for monthly, seasonal, annual instead of daily mean temperatures

Name: Maximum temperature
Definition: The maximum value of daily maximum temperature over a period (°C). In weather and climate models temperature is the variable simulating atmospheric air temperature at 2m above the surface. This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly values over a reference period.
Commentary: Like TXm, but for monthly, seasonal, annual instead of daily max temperatures

Name: Minimum temperature
Definition: The minimum value of daily minimum temperature over a period (°C). In weather and climate models temperature is the variable simulating atmospheric air temperature at 2m above the surface. This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly values over a reference period.
Commentary: Like TNm, but for monthly, seasonal, annual instead of daily min temperatures

Name: Maximum Consecutive Five-Day Precipitation
Definition: Maximum five days cumulated precipitation (mm). In weather and climate models total precipitation is the flux of water equivalent (rain or snow) reaching the land surface (expressed as kg.m-2.sec-2 and converted to mm/day). Precipitation is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly cumulated values over the considered period but extremes are cumulated on shorter periods (eg daily, 3-Day, or 5-days maximums).

Name: Extreme Precipitation Total
Definition: The total sum in a year of daily precipitation values exceeding the 95th percentile of the reference period (mm). In weather and climate models total precipitation is the flux of water equivalent (rain or snow) reaching the land surface (expressed as kg.m-2.sec-2 and converted to mm/day). Precipitation is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly cumulated values over the considered period but extremes are cumulated on shorter periods (eg daily, 3-Days, or 5-Days maximums).

Name: Extreme Precipitation Days
Definition: The count of days in a year with daily precipitation exceeding the 95th percentile threshold of rainy days over a reference period, here the 1981-2010 period (day). In weather and climate models total precipitation is the flux of water equivalent (rain or snow) reaching the land surface (expressed as kg.m-2.sec-2 and converted to mm day-1). This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly cumulated values over the considered period.

Name: Consecutive Dry Days
Definition: The longest period of consecutive days with daily precipitation below 1 mm in a year (day). In weather and climate models temperature is the variable simulating atmospheric air temperature at 2m above the surface. This Index is usually presented as annual, seasonal or monthly values over a reference period.

Name: Meteorological Drought Duration
Definition: The count of months in a year with anomalously low precipitation conditions based on the 3-month Standardised Precipitation Index (SPI-3) relative to a reference period, here 1981-2010 (month). A drought event starts when SPI-3 values fall below -1 for at least two consecutive months and ends when the index returns positive.

Name: Meteorological Drought Magnitude
Definition: The cumulative severity of drought events in a year based on the 3-month Standardised Precipitation Index (SPI-3) relative to a reference period, here 1981-2010 (dimensionless). A drought event starts when SPI-3 values fall below -1 for at least two consecutive months and ends when the index returns positive. The magnitude of the event is defined as the sum of SPI-3 absolute values in the months of the drought episode.

Name: River discharge
Definition: The River Discharge index is defined as the annual mean daily river discharge (m³⋅s⁻¹).
AssociatedVariable: pr, tas + sfcWind, rss, rls, psl, huss
Commentary: Output of a hydrological model; climate model variables used to drive the model are mentioned here: https://confluence.ecmwf.int/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=283549812#Hydrologyrelatedclimateimpactindicatorsfrom1970to2100derivedfrombiasadjustedEuropeanclimateprojections:ProductUserGuide,SpecificationandWorkflow-3.4InputdataInputdata

Name: River Flood
Definition: The River Flood index is the 50-year (also 10-, 5- and 2-year) flood recurrence value based on maximum river discharge. It is estimated from annual daily maximum river discharge using a Gumbel distribution.
AssociatedVariable: pr, tas + sfcWind, rss, rls, psl, huss
Commentary: Output of a hydrological model; climate model variables used to drive the model are mentioned here: https://confluence.ecmwf.int/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=283549812#Hydrologyrelatedclimateimpactindicatorsfrom1970to2100derivedfrombiasadjustedEuropeanclimateprojections:ProductUserGuide,SpecificationandWorkflow-3.4InputdataInputdata

Name: Aridity Actual
Definition: The ratio between mean annual actual evapotranspiration and mean annual precipitation, generally calculated over a reference period of 30 years. Actual evapotranspiration is estimated using hydrological models and, in contrast to potential evapotranspiration, accounts for the limited water content actually available in the soil when estimating the evapotranspiration demand.
AssociatedVariable: pr, evspsbl / pr, tas + sfcWind, huss, psl, rss, rsl
Commentary: Output of a hydrological model; climate model variables used to drive the model are mentioned here: https://confluence.ecmwf.int/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=283549812#Hydrologyrelatedclimateimpactindicatorsfrom1970to2100derivedfrombiasadjustedEuropeanclimateprojections:ProductUserGuide,SpecificationandWorkflow-3.4InputdataInputdata

Name: Mean Soil Moisture
Definition: The soil moisture is defined as the monthly mean values of soil moisture in the root zone as the fraction of the field capacity volume over a 30 year period.
AssociatedVariable: rzwc (Mass Content Of Water In Soil Layer Defined By Root Depth), mrsofc / pr, tas + sfcWind, rss, rls, psl, huss
Commentary: Output of a hydrological model; climate model variables used to drive the model are mentioned here: https://confluence.ecmwf.int/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=283549812#Hydrologyrelatedclimateimpactindicatorsfrom1970to2100derivedfrombiasadjustedEuropeanclimateprojections:ProductUserGuide,SpecificationandWorkflow-3.4InputdataInputdata

Name: High Fire Danger Days
Definition: The count of days in a period with a FWI value greater than 30 (Number of days) based upon the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) classification. The Fire Weather Index (FWI) is a meteorologically based index used worldwide to estimate fire danger. It is developed by the Canadian Forestry Service to estimate forest fire ignition and spread conditions based on several weather variables (temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and wind speed).

Name: Fire Weather Index
Definition: The Fire Weather Index (FWI) is a meteorologically based index used worldwide to estimate fire danger. It is developed by the Canadian Forestry Service to estimate forest fire ignition and spread conditions based on several weather variables (temperature, precipitation, relative humidity, and wind speed).
LinkedIndicators: Met Office Fire Danger, Wildfire: Daily Hazard Assessment; Wildfire: FFMC 99th percentile

Name: Mean Wind Speed
Definition: The mean daily 10m wind speed over a period (m s-1).

Name: Extreme Wind Days
Definition: The count of days in a year with daily 10m wind speed exceeding the 98th percentile threshold over a reference period, here the 1981-2010 period (days).

Name: Snowfall Amount
Definition: The Snowfall Amount index (mm) corresponds to the cumulative value of snowfall precipitation over the winter season from November to April.

Name: High Snow Days
Definition: The High Snow Days index (days) counts the number of days where the water equivalent of natural snow is above a given threshold (here 120 kg m-2) from august to july of the following year.

Name: Relative Sea Level Rise
Definition: The Relative Sea Level Rise index (cm) is the annual mean sea level height relative to the 1986-2005 period.
Commentary: Output of Global Tide and Surge Model (2D hydrodynamic model)

Name: Extreme Sea Level
Definition: The Extreme Sea Level index (m) is the Total water level value for a return period of 100 years caused by tidal and surge levels as well as their interactions but without including sea level rise.
Commentary: Output of Global Tide and Surge Model (2D hydrodynamic model); Return period of total water level (TWL), which includes annual sea level change, tides, storm surge

Name: Sea Surface Temperature
Definition: The Sea Surface Temperature index represents the mean sea surface temperature over different timescales (°C).

Name: Marine Heatwaves Days index (MHD)
Definition: The Marine Heatwaves Days index (MHD) is defined as the count of days under marine heatwaves conditions (days). A Marine Heatwave day is a day exceeding the daily climatological 90th percentile of SST during the May to September season and a reference period.

Name: Dissolved Oxygen Level
Definition: The Dissolved Oxygen Level index (mol / m³) is the concentration of dissolved oxygen at a certain depth. Oxygen concentrations above 190 mmol m³ are considered to be sufficient to support healthy marine communities with minimal problems, while oxygen concentrations below 62.5 mmol m³ are considered to be a source of serious concern.
Commentary: Output of ecosystem model: might require solar radiation and ocean absorption, wind, partial CO2 in air, nutrients and inflow of freshwater into ocean and other parameters to run

Name: Ocean pH level
Definition: The Ocean pH Level index (dimensionless) is the seawater pH at a certain depth. pH is a measure of the concentration of hydrogen ions in a solution. The more hydrogen ions that are present, the more acidic is the solution. The pH scale ranges from zero (very acidic) to 14 (very basic). The scale is logarithmic, meaning a single unit corresponds to a ten-fold difference. A pH of 7 is neutral, a pH less than 7 is acidic, and a pH greater than 7 is basic.
AssociatedVariable: ph + (sometimes evaluated: spco2, spco2abio, spco2nat, dpco2, dpco2abio, dpco2nat, talk, talknat, dissic, dissicabio, dissicnat)
Commentary: Output of ecosystem model

Name: Tiger Mosquito Climatic Suitability
Definition: The Climatic Suitability index of Tiger mosquito (Aedes albopictus) presence (Dimensionless, from 0 to 100). The Tiger Mosquito Climatic Suitability index is relevant to human health. The tiger mosquito is an invasive species from south-east Asia favoured by a warmer climate and represents a serious threat as it transmits vector-borne diseases such as dengue and chikungunya. Environmental factors, among which weather conditions, affect both the potential presence and seasonal activity of the tiger mosquito. The Tiger mosquito's climatic suitability is determined by summer temperatures, January temperatures and annual rainfall. The suitability is null for summer temperatures lower than 15°C or higher than 30°C, with a maximum between 20°C and 25°C. It is null for January temperatures lower than - 1°C and annual rainfall lower than 450 mm, and maximal for January temperatures above 3°C and annual rainfall above 800 mm.

Name: Tiger Mosquito Climatic Season Length
Definition: The season length of the climatic suitability of tiger mosquito presence (Days). The Tiger mosquito's climatic suitability seasonal presence is determined by temperature thresholds and hours of sunlight (photoperiod) during spring (when egg hatching occurs) and autumn (a period of suspended development or diapause). In spring the temperature should be above 10.5°C and the photoperiod above 11.25 hours and in autumn the temperature should be below 9.5°C and the photoperiod below 13.5 hours. The latter is conditioned by the ability of the mosquito to survive the winter combined with a threshold on annual rainfall. Survival conditions are considered as unsuitable for January temperatures below 0°C and annual rainfall below 500 mm.

Name: Consecutive Summer Days (CSD)
Definition: Let TX_ij be the daily maximum temperature at day i of period j. Then counted is the largest number of consecutive days where daily maximum temperature exceeds 25 degrees Celsius (TX_ij > 25).

Name: Consecutive Frost Days (CFD)
Definition: Let TX_ij be the daily maximum temperature at day i of period j. Then counted is the largest number of consecutive days where daily maximum temperature is less than 0 degrees Celsius (TX_ij < 0).

Name: Potential Evapotranspiration (PET: Penman-Monteith)
Definition: PET is an index which gives the FAO-endorsed potential evapotranspiration as calculated by the Penman-Monteith parametrization. Here reference crop evapotranspiration is a measure for potential evapotranspiration. Reference crop evaporation is defined as the rate of evaporation from an idealized grass reference crop with a fixed crop height of 0.12 m, an albedo of 0.23, and a surface resistance of 70 s m−1 . In terms of of its evaporation rate, such a crop closely resembles the reference crop of an extensive surface of short green grass cover of uniform height, actively growing, completely shading the ground, and not short of water.
AssociatedVariable: tas, hurs, psl, rss, rls, sfcWind

Name: Potential Evapotranspiration (PET: Makkink)
Definition: This formulation of Reference Evapotranspiration is a simplification of the more comprehensive Penman-Monteith parameterization and recognizes that evapotranspiration is determined primarily by the radiation and the ambient air temperature. A further simplification is that Global Radiation is used rather than the net radiation which is used in more comprehensive formulas.

Name: Self-calibrating Palmer Drought Severity Index (scPDSI)
Definition:
The Palmer Drought Severity Index (PDSI) is a measure of regional moisture availability that has been used extensively to study droughts and wet spells in the contiguous USA. The computation of the index involves a classification of relative moisture conditions within 11 categories as defined by Palmer (1965), ranging from extremely dry with PDSI, to extremely wet with PDSI values. The index is based on water supply and demand which is calculated using a water-budget system based on historic records of precipitation and temperature and the soil characteristics of the site being considered. 
The scPDSI as put forward by Wells et al. (2004) is more appropriate for geographical comparison of climates of diverse regions. Wells et al. (2004) improve the performance of the PDSI by automating the calculations Palmer made when he derived the empirical constants used in the PDSI algorithm.

Name: Huglin Index
Definition: The Huglin Index is an index specifically aimed at grap growth and defined using daily averaged temperature TG_i and the daily maximum temperature TX_i for day i in the period 1 April to 30 September: K/2 * SUM((TG_i - 10) + (TX_i - 10)), where K is a daylength coefficient. The daylight coefficient is a function of the latitude of the station but a clear definition is absent. The value of K is 1 (<= 40°N) or 1.02 (40-42°N), increasing at increment of 0.01 for each 2 degrees of latitude until 50°N and reaching 1.06.

Name: altCSDI
Definition: Similar to CSDI. For CSDI, the spells cannot span years, while for altCSDI the spells can span years.

Name: altWSDI
Definition: Similar to WSDI. For WSDI, the spells cannot span years, while for altWSDI the spells can span years.

Name: altCDD
Definition: Similar to CDD. For CDD, the spells can span years, while for altCDD the spells cannot span years.

Name: altCWD
Definition: Similar to CWD. For CWD, the spells can span years, while for altCWD the spells cannot span years.
